project: Namias Portfolio - Facebook Messenger Chat Integration
summary: Build a first-class in-site conversation surface that blends the existing AI chat with a Facebook Messenger handoff, so visitors can start on the portfolio and continue the conversation in Messenger without leaving the experience prematurely.
narrative: The portfolio already has a helpful AI chat widget and Messenger deep links, but the current experience is still split across buttons and contact cards. This PRD turns that into a coherent chat entry point inside the website itself: the AI panel becomes the primary conversation surface, Messenger becomes the real human handoff path, and the contact flow explains the difference between a Facebook account/profile link and the embedded Messenger product. One important constraint shapes the plan: Meta's customer chat plugin is designed for Facebook Pages, so a personal Facebook account can be surfaced through Messenger deep links and open-in-app handoff, but a full embedded Page plugin is only possible if the owner later creates or attaches a Page. The implementation therefore delivers the best possible in-site experience now, while keeping a future Page-based upgrade path explicit.
principles: Chat first, button second — visitors should see a conversation surface inside the website, not a scattered set of outbound links.
Respect platform constraints — personal Facebook accounts can be linked through Messenger, but the embedded customer chat plugin requires a Facebook Page.
Keep the AI assistant — Messenger handoff should extend the existing AI chat, not replace it.
Stay in the same shell — the chat experience should feel integrated with the current hub and contact UI.
Explain the path clearly — visitors should know when they are chatting with the site assistant and when they are handing off to Messenger.
Validate every slice — each implementation step must pass lint and build before it is committed.

epics.title: Messenger capability audit
epics.summary: Confirm how the existing Facebook account/profile can be surfaced through the website, document the Page-only limitation for Meta's embedded chat plugin, and define the exact in-site fallback that ships first.

stories.title: Normalize Messenger URLs and naming
stories.details: Use the Facebook account/profile URL https://www.facebook.com/jhon.keneth.namias.2024 and the Messenger deep link https://m.me/jhon.keneth.namias.2024 consistently across the project.

stories.title: Document the Page-only embedded chat constraint
stories.details: Add owner-facing guidance that explains the Meta customer chat plugin requirement so the code does not promise a feature that needs a Facebook Page.

epics.title: In-site chat surface
epics.summary: Turn the existing AI chat panel into a richer conversation hub by adding a dedicated Messenger handoff section, better labels, and a clear distinction between AI help and direct human messaging.

stories.title: Add a Messenger section to the chat panel
stories.details: Add a visible Messenger block inside the existing AI chat panel with a short explanation, the Facebook account link, and a direct message CTA.

stories.title: Keep AI and Messenger actions together
stories.details: Make the chat panel feel like one integrated flow so visitors can ask the AI first and escalate to Messenger without hunting through the rest of the site.

stories.title: Maintain accessible fallback links
stories.details: Keep the Messenger CTA keyboard-friendly, explicit, and safe for opening in a new tab or app.

epics.title: Copy, setup guide, and verification
epics.summary: Update the surrounding copy to say 'account' rather than 'page', add a concise owner setup guide, and verify the final implementation with lint and build checks.

stories.title: Update surrounding Facebook wording
stories.details: Change the connect and contact copy so it clearly says Facebook account/profile where appropriate and does not imply a Page unless one exists.

stories.title: Write the owner setup guide
stories.details: Provide a practical guide for enabling Messenger handoff, checking the Facebook account link, and later upgrading to a Page-based embedded chat if desired.

stories.title: Run lint and build
stories.details: Verify the messenger chat slice with npm run lint and npm run build before each commit.

ownerSetupGuide: Use the existing Facebook account/profile URL https://www.facebook.com/jhon.keneth.namias.2024 as the human-contact identity for the website.
Keep the Messenger deep link https://m.me/jhon.keneth.namias.2024 enabled so visitors can jump into a Messenger thread from the portfolio.
If you want a true embedded customer chat widget inside the site, create or attach a Facebook Page later because Meta's customer chat plugin is Page-based.
For the current release, prefer the in-site chat panel plus Messenger handoff over a standalone outbound button.
After each slice, validate with lint and build, then commit the slice by itself so the history stays easy to review.
